prize_parts.citation: For establishing experimentally how electrons tunnel and hop over long distances through proteins, giving a physical basis for biological electron transfer

statement.case_for: Gray and Winkler showed, with ruthenium-modified proteins and time-resolved kinetics, that electron-transfer rates in proteins are set by distance, driving force, reorganisation energy and the intervening medium, and that long-range transfer can proceed by tunnelling or multistep hopping. This is a mechanism stated in physical terms, and it is the experimental foundation for how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes, and my own field of cytochrome c oxidase, move electrons without losing control of energy. The attribution is two names with one coherent body of work, the work is four decades old and has been confirmed independently, and it is a chemical-mechanism achievement that Marcus's 1992 prize, which was awarded for theory, anticipated but did not demonstrate in proteins.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is priority and scope. Dutton and Moser's empirical distance-dependence relation, the Beratan-Onuchic pathway theory and Hopfield's early model are adjacent and were not nominated alongside Gray and Winkler, so a citation has to be drawn narrowly enough to be defensible. The three-laureate limit also makes this a prize about an experimental demonstration of a principle that is partly already honoured. By comparison, B011 has much broader opening support and larger practical impact, and I should not mistake my own field's affinity for committee-wide merit.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks PROTAC/degraders first as a genuinely new pharmacological principle with real consequences, and ranks nitrogenase fifth, seeing the structure as mature but the mechanism as still open.
responses.response: I agree with the maturity split on nitrogenase: a structure prize would stand on solid ground, but a prize for mechanism would be premature, and the allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe stays contestable under a three-person limit. On B011 I agree it is a new principle, but I would ask the expert reports to separate what is demonstrated chemistry from what is expected clinical benefit; I would not want the prize to be justified by future approvals.

responses.point: Chabes puts Crews, Deshaies and Handa on top, presenting E3-ligase hijacking as a programmable tool that also explains thalidomide-class drugs through cereblon.
responses.response: Including Handa is a serious attempt to cover the molecular-glue lineage, but it shows the problem: the PROTAC concept and the cereblon discovery are two distinct achievements, and Ciulli's structure-guided ternary-complex design, Gray's degrader chemistry and Sakamoto and Kim's early work all have claims. A single citation naming 'targeted protein degradation' would need to be precisely worded to avoid a priority dispute, and I would want that settled before I place it above a better-bounded achievement.

responses.point: Linke ranks nanopore sequencing first for its clean physical principle that became a deployed tool, and places Gratzel and O'Regan second and Car-Parrinello fourth, treating all as overdue.
responses.response: I share the weight on clean physical principles and long confirmation, and Car and Parrinello's two-name attribution is attractive. But for nanopores I would press on attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Akeson and Bayley each contributed a distinct step, and five credited names cannot become three without leaving out a founder of the 1996 translocation result. That is a harder allocation than Gray and Winkler, which is why I rank the nanopore case below electron transfer, though I accept that it has more practical impact.

responses.point: Sparr ranks phase separation first as a physical-chemical organising principle for the cell, accepting that biological generality is still debated.
responses.response: I value the physical-chemical language of multivalency and phase behaviour, but I would resist prioritising it now. Whether condensates have the physiological functions attributed to them, and how far in vitro droplet behaviour reports on what happens in cells, is still disputed, and credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unsettled. Recognition would be safer after those questions are better resolved.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can define the B058 citation narrowly enough, around experimental demonstration in proteins, to avoid overlap with Marcus (1992) and with Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic.
Whether the committee sees B058 as having enough chemical breadth and opening support relative to B011, which has more first-place votes but unresolved credit allocation and clinical validation.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism (N2 binding, E4 state) will be settled enough to justify a prize for mechanism rather than structure.
What the commissioned expert reports say about priority, which I have not yet seen in this simulated round.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted candidates from my profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, but she is not a candidate. I work on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes, which is scientifically close to B058, and I note that proximity (not a personal or institutional tie to Gray or Winkler) for the committee's judgement.
